handoff.purpose: Kairos bounded scheduler: accept/plan/dispatch/gate writes with concurrency caps and safety policy

claims.text: Kairos never talks to the user, never decides trust, and bounces anything that belongs to the senior crew back to the trusted orchestration layer.
claims.why: accept() routes via route_and_select and bounces non-FREE_LANES; no user I/O; trust decisions delegated to Policy and route_and_select

claims.text: dynamically spawns local workers from a bounded pool (the Mexican/Italian Ollama bench; the Chinese DeepSeek bench stays dormant without a key)
claims.why: _bench = cycle(roster('ollama')) and DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY has deepseek False; pool bounded by max_workers

claims.text: briefs each with a scoped task + the owning specialist's domain
claims.why: Assignment carries objective, paths, owner, worker, lane

claims.text: enforces their *reduced rights* (the Ollama write-guard already refuses device/vendor/secret/high-risk paths)
claims.why: write-guard enforcement lives in offload/provider layer, not in this chunk

claims.text: returns a consolidated report for Adam / the owning specialist to review
claims.why: dispatch returns results list with per-assignment status/wrote/result

claims.text: This is not a proof of write isolation: an agent may touch an undeclared path. Production write concurrency therefore remains disabled until each task owns a separate Forge workcell/worktree.
claims.why: _paths_overlap only checks declared hints; dispatch keeps writes sequential unless no writes; parallel only for advisory

claims.text: Concurrency cap SPECIFICALLY for gate_concurrent_writes ... independent of max_workers
claims.why: max_parallel_writes is a separate field from max_workers

claims.text: every concurrent write-mode offload() triggers a FULL structcore re-index (offload.py's post-write blast-radius fence, cached_index(..., refresh=True))
claims.why: offload.py internals not in this chunk

claims.text: cache's single-flight lock is keyed by RESOLVED ROOT ... N worktrees, N distinct roots, N UNSHARED full re-index builds
claims.why: structcore/index.py not in this chunk

claims.text: NOT MEASURED on this box for N>1 -- the default stays low until someone measures the real cost and raises it deliberately
claims.why: max_parallel_writes default is 2; no measurement code present

claims.text: Extra pool workers Ikarus can spin up for fan-out beyond the role shadows
claims.why: _bench cycle from roster('ollama') provides extra personas

claims.text: Only low-risk work that Adam would offload is taken; anything that routes back to Claude is bounced to Adam
claims.why: decision.provider not in FREE_LANES -> bounced Assignment with accepted=False

claims.text: repo_root makes the target repo's own .agentenv/agents/ roster visible to routing (without it only global agents route)
claims.why: routing logic in route_and_select; this chunk only forwards repo_root

claims.text: Dry run: who gets spawned, in how many bounded waves
claims.why: plan calls accept and computes waves = ceil(len(taken)/max_workers)

claims.text: dry_run stops at the spawn plan; live actually invokes each bench worker through the provider seam
claims.why: _bounced_or_planned returns status 'planned' when dry_run; live path calls offload()

claims.text: Sequential by default (parallel=False): each live write is verified by diffing a WHOLE-repo content-hash snapshot around that one run (offload._repo_snapshot)
claims.why: offload._repo_snapshot not in this chunk; dispatch passes isolate=False for sequential runs

claims.text: two such runs on one repo concurrently would cross-attribute disk_changed
claims.why: offload behavior not in this chunk

claims.text: parallel=True currently overlaps advisory-only work
claims.why: can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes; has_writes true if any write mode

claims.text: Declared path disjointness is not a security boundary: a writable agent can touch an undeclared repository path
claims.why: _paths_overlap only checks declared paths; dispatch does not use it to allow parallel writes

claims.text: Writable concurrency stays sequential with whole-repository snapshots until Forge gives every attempt its own workcell/worktree
claims.why: can_parallel false when has_writes; writes run sequentially

claims.text: Only read-only/advisory attempts may share a checkout concurrently. Pairwise-disjoint declared strings are not evidence that agentic writers stay within those strings.
claims.why: can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes; no disjointness check used

claims.text: Writes may go parallel ONLY when each one gets its own worktree
claims.why: parallel path passes isolate=True to _run_one; but only when no writes, so this claim describes gate_concurrent_writes path

claims.text: STILL sequential here, but the reason changed: the isolation now EXISTS -- see gate_concurrent_writes() below, which runs each write through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt (its own worktree, its own hardened patch capture) fanned out concurrently
claims.why: TaskAttempt behavior not in this chunk; gate_concurrent_writes only defined here, not executed

claims.text: daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates(), which lands gated candidates one at a time behind a cross-process lock with cumulative re-gating
claims.why: gated_writes module not in this chunk

claims.text: What THAT path returns is not what this one returns, though: a gated PatchArtifact the primary checkout never saw, not a live write already sitting in repo_root's working tree
claims.why: gated_writes return shape not in this chunk

claims.text: dispatch() keeps its existing auto-land contract for a single write (offload() has always auto-landed a sequential one)
claims.why: offload auto-land behavior not in this chunk

claims.text: does not silently switch write-mode dispatch to the gated-candidate shape
claims.why: dispatch never calls gate_concurrent_writes; it calls offload directly for sequential writes

claims.text: Call gate_concurrent_writes()/promote_candidates() explicitly when that decision says to.
claims.why: dispatch does not call them; explicit call required by user

claims.text: Safe concurrent WRITE dispatch: PHASE 1 only (gating, not landing)
claims.why: method body is truncated; only signature and docstring visible

claims.text: Every write task in tasks runs CONCURRENTLY, each through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt in its own worktree (offload() as the runner -- its verify+rollback cascade stays the authority for per-task correctness; see daedalus.kairos.gated_writes._relay_gate)
claims.why: body not in chunk; TaskAttempt and _relay_gate not visible

claims.text: Returns one daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.GatedCandidate per accepted write task: a gate verdict plus a PatchArtifact when clean
claims.why: body not in chunk; return type not observable

claims.text: The primary checkout at repo_root is NEVER touched by this call -- that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee (see tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_happy_path_artifact_and_primary_untouched)
claims.why: TaskAttempt and test not in chunk

claims.text: Advisory-only tasks are bounced (this method only accepts write-mode work; use plan/accept for the routing verdict on the rest of a mixed task list, or dispatch to actually run them)
claims.why: body not in chunk; bounce logic not visible

claims.text: cancel, when given, is forwarded unchanged to [rest truncated]
claims.why: docstring truncated; forwarding not observable

observations.what: gate_concurrent_writes is defined but its body is entirely truncated; all claims about its behavior are uncheckable from this chunk
dispatch has a long comment block describing a design decision but the code itself does not implement the gated path; it only notes the decision
_paths_overlap is defined but never used in this chunk; it is a diagnostic helper only
max_parallel_writes is set but never used in this chunk; only gate_concurrent_writes would use it
The _bench cycle is created but never used in this chunk; it is presumably used by provider spawning elsewhere
accept() accesses t['objective'] directly; if a task dict lacks 'objective', KeyError propagates (no guard)
dispatch() uses 'parallel and not has_writes' to decide can_parallel; if has_writes is true, parallel is silently downgraded to sequential with a note appended

risks: line 105 | medium | accept() unguarded t['objective'] subscript; malformed task dict raises KeyError with no repair | add a .get with default or catch KeyError and reject task
